subject: Heartland onboarding: quota tempo sync & launch signal plan
messages:
From: Kate Morris <kate@heartland.app>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Heartland launch: expected traffic and temporary quota ask

Hi Tessa,

We’re ramping toward a limited public beta on 2026-09-14 and need to lock in a temporary uplift for token throughput during the first 72 hours. Forecast attached — expect a 6x spike from baseline, mostly reads for generation with a ~40 token average. Ops wants confirmation by EOD Wed so we can finalize our release checklist.

Specific asks:
- Temporary quota bump to 12M tokens/day for 9/14–9/16
- Short-term increase to concurrent requests from 200 -> 600
- A fallback/route policy if latency rises above 200ms

Can you confirm feasibility and any product asks we should prepare for?

Thanks,
Kate
Head of Product, Heartland
[attachment: heartland_launch_forecast.csv (CSV)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morris <kate@heartland.app>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Heartland launch: expected traffic and temporary quota ask

Hi Kate — thanks for the forecast. I’ve looped in Karthik (infra) and Marcus (dedicated ops) to validate capacity and routing options. High-level: we can usually support short 3-day uplifts with a dedicated quota window and route policy, but need confirmation on request concurrency shape and early spike shape (first 3 hours vs steady).

Would you be able to share minute-level ingress for the peak hour(s)? That’ll determine whether we recommend a soft ramp or a single step increase. I’ll also attach a mutual action plan draft and SOW preview for approvals.

Next steps:
- Heartland: minute-level peak for peak day(s) + call availability for Wed 9/2 09:00 PT
- Redwood: internal capacity check + recommended rate-limit window by EOD Wed

Best,
Tessa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Heartland launch: capacity check + product asks

Tessa / Marcus — quick infra read: based on the CSV, the 6x daily jump concentrated into a 2-hour window will stress our serving pools if we leave default batching. Two immediate product-level asks to reduce risk:

1) Enable prefix KV caching for Heartland’s most common prompts (they reported ~20 prompt templates). This reduces per-token compute on the hot path.
2) Apply a temporary lower-precision quantization variant (q4f16) for the dedicated pool serving Heartland for those 72 hours — quality tests show negligible delta for current prompts.

Operational notes:
- We can provision the quota window (12M tokens/day) and increase concurrent request allowance to 600, but we need an SLA exception signed for the burst and an on-call rotation for the peak day.
- If Heartland can accept a 15-minute soft-ramp (linear window) for the first hour, we can avoid a large cold-KV penalty.

I’ll put a tentative routing policy and rollback policy in the drive folder. Marcus — any capacity objections?

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Heartland launch: capacity check + product asks

On Thu, Sep 2, 2026 at 09:12, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tessa / Marcus — quick infra read: based on the CSV, the 6x daily jump concentrated into a 2-hour window will stress our serving pools if we leave default batching. Two immediate product-level asks to reduce risk:

Thanks — confirmed. We can support the requested 12M tokens/day with the following guardrails:
- Dedicated pool allocation: reserve 30% headroom beyond forecast to handle bursts (provisioned pool: 15 GPUs with auto-burst off)
- Temporary routing policy: route to q4f16 variant first, fallback to full-precision only if quality regressions exceed thresholds
- On-call schedule: Marcus (primary), Neha (secondary), Karthik (infra) for 9/14 00:00–23:59 PT

One ask for sales/legal: need formal sign-off on the SLA exception wording (we’ll allow a single-day spike waiver for tail latency) and DocuSign executed before we flip the quota. Also confirm whether Heartland will run a smoke test 48 hours prior so we can validate the KV warm cache.

I set tentative DocuSign link in the drive.

—Marcus
Manager, Dedicated Capacity Operations

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morris <kate@heartland.app>, ops+heartland@heartland.app
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Heartland launch: quota tempo sync & launch signal plan

Hi all — quick summary and asks so we have a single thread for approvals: 

Summary:
- Redwood can provide the temporary quota bump to 12M tokens/day for 9/14–9/16 and raise concurrent requests to 600.
- Product/infra recommends enabling KV prefix caching + serving q4f16 variant during the window; they’ll monitor quality metrics and rollback if needed.
- On-call rota: Marcus (primary), Neha (secondary), Karthik (infra) for the peak day.

Action items:
- Heartland: sign the SLA exception and SOW preview in DocuSign (link in Drive) by 9/10 EOD.
- Heartland: run a 30-minute smoke test on 9/12 to warm caches and share minute-level ingress for peak hour(s) by 9/9.
- Redwood: provision the dedicated pool and prepare routing policy; Karthik to post the final playbook by 9/10.

If you’re good with the above, I’ll route to Legal for the final SLA language and schedule the DocuSign.

Thanks — excited to see Heartland go live.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
